subject: Request: short-term capacity bump & billing path for June surge
messages:
From: Javier Ortiz <javier.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Urgent: we’re hitting quota — need capacity bump & billing options

Hi Aisha / Karthik,

Quick note from our ops team: we started a phased rollout of clinical note-generation yesterday and are already hitting our soft quota limits. This is impacting a small subset of production traffic (estimated 18% of requests getting throttled). We expect the next 72 hours to be highest risk as the pilot ramps.

Can Redwood provision a short-term capacity bump or temporary override so we avoid dropping requests? From a procurement perspective, we’re flexible on how you want to bill (one-off invoice, provisional credit, or staged billing) but need clarity on the path and timeline.

Attached is a quick projection of expected weekly token volume and the SOW draft we used internally. Please advise next steps and whether we need a formal PO today.

Thanks,
Javier
Director, Platform Ops
Acme Health

Attachments: billing_projection.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW_draft_Acme_v2.pdf (draft SOW)

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: Javier Ortiz <javier.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: we’re hitting quota — need capacity bump & billing options

Hi Javier,

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the projection. We can support a short-term "soft-cap exception" that will: 1) temporarily raise your request rate by X TPS for up to 7 days, and 2) enable a provisional billing path so you aren’t blocked while procurement finalizes paperwork.

Options we typically offer for a situation like this:
- "Grace window" override + provisional invoice: immediate capacity bump, one-time provisional invoice for the estimated overrun, settled at month-end with final true-up.
- Staged billing (preferred for pilots): defer 50% of overrun to next invoice and apply a one-time credit if total runs are within projected bounds.
- Short-term committed uplift: convert the temporary headroom into a 1-month add-on at a discounted uplift rate (requires PO).

To proceed I need: the expected peak tokens/day (you can use the spreadsheet), whether you need the override immediately (we can enable within 2 hours), and the preferred billing path. I’ve looped in Karthik to help with pricing specifics.

If you want, we can do a 20-minute call now to lock this down.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Aisha Rahman
Redwood Inference

Aisha, thanks.

We did a quick re-run of the projection and attached a small update (same file). Expected peak tokens/day for the next 3 days: ~1.6M (versus our baseline of 0.9M). We need the override immediately; throttling is degrading the pilot experience.

Procurement: if Redwood can do a provisional invoice + true-up at month end, and provide a short-term credit if actual usage does not exceed projections by >10%, that should be acceptable. We’ll follow up with a PO by EOD if that helps.

Javier

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Javier Ortiz <javier.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: we’re hitting quota — need capacity bump & billing options

Hi all,

We enabled a provisional soft-cap exception for Acme Health at 14:30 ET yesterday; the elevated throughput is active and should remove the throttles you saw. Per Aisha’s note, here’s the proposed billing path to keep things simple and low-friction:

1) Temporary uplift active for up to 7 days to cover the pilot surge.
2) Redwood will issue a provisional invoice for estimated overrun (based on your projection).
3) We will apply a 25% discount on overrun charges for the first billing cycle as a pilot concession.
4) A final true-up will occur at month-end; if actual usage is below projected by >10%, we will issue a credit equal to the prorated overrun amount less the 25% concession.

Caveats: discounts apply only to non-negotiable overrun charges and do not affect base committed pricing. This uplift does not modify SLA guarantees; prolonged high throughput should be moved to a short-term commit for reliability.

Next steps: if procurement can share a PO number (or confirm they will accept a provisional invoice), we’ll attach an updated SOW and DocuSign link for signature. Otherwise, the provisional invoice will be sent to procurement@acmehealth.com and flagged as "pending PO".

Karthik, please confirm the dollar estimate we should use for the provisional invoice (I used the updated projection as a baseline).

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
